copy.intro: Community demos and informal evaluations attributed by their publishers to Kimi K3.1, including the anonymous Kibitz checkpoint.
copy.purpose: Explore concrete tasks, visible outputs and practical limits through their original sources.
copy.stats: 40 independent usecases across 6 categories. Reposts and comparisons of the same work are grouped together.
copy.evidence: The Kibitz–Kimi K3.1 mapping is unconfirmed. Model names, timings, costs and quality judgments are source-reported. Recordings do not establish runnable code, complete interaction or repeatable success.
copy.steps:
1. Choose a task in the Menu.
2. Open its video or image, then follow the source-linked case title.
3. Compare the visible result with the stated task and limitations.
copy.thanks: Thanks to the publishers whose demonstrations make this collection possible:
copy.corrections: Attribution follows the linked sources and may need correction. Please open an issue for missing credit, duplicate work, inaccurate claims or removal requests. Third-party media retains its original ownership.

cases: 3D printer comparison
Compare a mechanical printer scene across two model recordings.
The creator shows a green-frame 3D printer; a later Carbon comparison revisits this work. The ranking is the creator's judgment.
Eden Ark mechanical scene
Inspect geometry and presentation in a mechanical scene comparison.
The recording labels Kibitz as rumored Kimi K3.1 and compares it with Kalmia. The creator prefers the Kibitz result.
Detailed wristwatch
Inspect a watch model's materials, lighting and dial details.
The attached recording shows a detailed watch. The creator describes it as a Three.js result; no controlled comparison is provided.
BMW M5 configurator
Explore a car prototype with color, door and camera controls.
The author reports colors, doors, lights, camera views and live rev mode from one prompt, calling Kibitz most likely Kimi K3.1.
Konark sundial wheel
Compare decorative detail with the functional requirement of telling time.
The creator favors Gemini's carvings and Opus's timekeeping, describing Kimi's wheel as simpler. These are source-reported judgments.
Interactive Xbox controller
Inspect a controller prototype and its on-screen controls.
The creator attributes the interactive Xbox-style controller to Kibitz on Arena. The recording shows the controller and interface.
Interactive steam train
Explore speed controls, exploded views and wireframe presentation.
The source reports a working train with a speed slider, assembly views, wireframe and statistics. A repost uses the same video.
Helicopter assembly and flight
Compare takeoff, landing and exploded views in helicopter prototypes.
The sources report roughly 15–20 minutes per model. The comparison author finds Qwen more realistic; both outputs remain visible.
Chimera phoenix
Inspect an elaborate creature model and its presentation.
The recording shows a colorful creature titled The Chimera Phoenix. The author reports mixed results across other tests.
Clockwork house comparison
Compare a small mechanical house with Fable's result.
The creator compares Kibitz with Fable 5.1 and reports faster generation in this test. The broader quality ranking is subjective.
Grassy hill and tree
Inspect a scene the creator presents as reverse engineering.
The attached recording shows a grassy hill, a tree and time-of-day controls. Release-date and price predictions are not treated as facts.
Japanese temple game asset
Inspect a temple asset with cherry blossoms and layered geometry.
The creator presents the temple as a 3D game asset from Kibitz. A separate still from their earlier post shows another view.
Kitchen with interactive refrigerator
Explore a kitchen prototype with an opening refrigerator.
The creator says the dining-room and refrigerator task took about an hour. A separate still shows the refrigerator interior.
Kitchen scene evaluation
Inspect a kitchen layout while separating visuals from functionality.
The creator calls this one of their strongest kitchen-test results, behind Fable 5.5. This collection has not run the scene.
Low-poly Japanese train station
Inspect a code-generated station with stylized landscaping.
The creator requests a low-poly Japanese train station and says no models or images were used. The model attribution remains tentative.
Voxel cherry-blossom valley
Compare two voxel valley outputs from the same requested scene.
The author compares Qwen 4 with source-attributed Kimi K3.1. Their earlier Kibitz recording supplies a separate view of the valley.
Castle above the clouds
Inspect a floating castle scene and its atmosphere.
The creator says they built the castle with Kibitz on Arena. The recording shows the castle, clouds and a moonlit sky.
Medieval voxel castle
Inspect a stylized castle and surrounding voxel landscape.
The attached recording shows a medieval voxel castle. Similarity to other models is an opinion, not evidence of shared training.
Mechanical diorama comparison
Inspect two intricate scenes from an Arena trial.
The source records a personal Arena trial and shows paired mechanical environments. The full prompt and functional checks are not disclosed.
Castle with dragons and windmill
Inspect a castle scene with several animated elements.
The author reports dragons, a windmill, roaming animals, a moat and drawbridge, generated in about 20 minutes. Reposts are grouped here.
Voxel pagoda across models
Compare a pagoda scene with several frontier-model outputs.
The original pagoda and a later comparison are kept together. Visual similarity does not establish model identity or distillation.
Sunset pagoda and comparisons
Compare one pagoda work with Qwen and Opus examples.
The author's pagoda recording and two comparison recordings belong to one work. They are not three independent case studies.
Pastel pagoda
Inspect a softly colored pagoda scene from Kibitz.
The source explicitly says Kibitz is only suspected to be Kimi K3.1. The recording also includes a model self-identification, which is unreliable.
Stacked pelican composition
Compare a layered controller, bicycle and pelican scene.
The creator labels the outputs Kimi K3.1 Pro and Fable 5.5. Those are source labels; this does not confirm a Pro edition.
Controller and pelican stack
Inspect a complex stacking instruction and its spatial relationships.
The source describes a controller, bicycle and pelican stack. Later screenshots compare it with GPT-6 Sol; a repost is grouped here.
Pelican bicycle animation
Inspect a cycling pelican animation and its interface.
The creator records a GIF from a Kibitz test. The Chinese-interface composition is a distinct work from the other pelican cases.
Pelican bicycle comparison
Compare two responses to a pelican-riding-a-bicycle request.
The author presents source-attributed Kimi K3.1 and Qwen 4 outputs side by side. The post asks readers to judge the result.
Moon and star field
Inspect an animated celestial drawing from a reported one-shot test.
The creator describes the result as JavaScript drawing. The recording shows a moon and star field; speed claims remain source-reported.
Interactive pelican SVG
Inspect cycling controls, annotations and SVG export in a vector scene.
The original creator provides a public SVG request. Reposts add descriptions of cadence, lighting and export controls; no prompt is reconstructed here.
Ana de Armas SVG portrait
Inspect a portrait while keeping generation effort visible.
The author reports about 49k tokens, 22 minutes, max effort and zero-shot generation. The later post repeats the Kimi portrait and adds a GPT-6 Astra TiKZ comparison.
Portrait SVG comparison
Compare portrait drawings with their anonymous checkpoint labels visible.
The screenshot labels the left result Kibitz and the right Kalmia. The source discusses SVG drawing; neither official model mapping is confirmed.
Backrooms game comparison
Compare game outputs while retaining the creator's negative experience.
The author reports 40 minutes for Kimi and 1 hour 1 minute for Opus, and says they are disappointed with the Kimi game result.
RPG village and dragon raid
Compare a village scene with weather and day–night behavior.
The author reports working dragon raids, thunderstorms and day–night cycles in both outputs, with roughly 15 minutes generation each.
Airplane takeoff and landing
Inspect a flight-game prototype with a runway.
The source reports a playable one-shot airplane game with takeoff and landing in about 10 minutes. This collection has not tested playability.
Chai and paratha cafe menu
Inspect a single-page menu for a local cafe.
The author asks allegedly Kimi K3.1 to build a Pakistani chai and paratha cafe menu. Training-origin speculation is excluded from the takeaway.
Giraffe model comparison
Compare four giraffe outputs with their displayed model labels.
The author compares Opus 5.5, Carbon, Kibitz and Kalmia, preferring Gemini. These are informal Arena results, not a controlled benchmark.
Horse model comparison
Inspect how three outputs handle the same visible subject.
The recording compares horse scenes labeled Carbon, Opus 5.5 and Kimi K3.1. The author's ranking is an opinion about this sample.
Bicycle and cow spatial test
Check whether the output preserves an unusual subject–object instruction.
The request asks for a bicycle riding a cow. The creator notes that Kimi appears to correct the instruction; a later Carbon result is attached.
Animal bicycle scene comparison
Compare two animal-and-bicycle scenes with anonymous labels.
The source compares Kalmia and Kibitz while making conflicting guesses about their Kimi identities. Those guesses are not adopted as facts.
Minecraft self-portrait
Compare Minecraft-style self-portraits while checking cost evidence separately.
The source reports 13,707 blocks and $0.38 versus 5,738 blocks and $5.31. Billing, token scope and retry costs were not independently verified.
